headline_marked: ICT to deliver [[verdict on Rampura cornice shooting]] and killings today
headline: ICT to deliver verdict on Rampura cornice shooting and killings today
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal will rule on crimes against humanity involving the shooting of a youth hanging from a building's cornice and two other deaths during the 2024 July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) is set to deliver its verdict today in a case involving crimes against humanity during the 2024 July Uprising in Dhaka's Rampura. The case centers on the shooting and killing of two people and the serious injury of another.
The charges involve five police officers, including former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman. While ASI Chanchal Chandra Sarkar is currently in jail, the other four accused officers are absconding.
One charge details the death of 38-year-old Md Nadeem, who was killed on July 19 when police opened fire indiscriminately in Banasree H Block. He was hit by two bullets in the stomach and back.

Another charge involves 18-year-old Amir Hossain, who sought shelter in an under-construction building to escape police fire. He was shot six times while hanging from a roof rod (cornice) after refusing to jump down.

A third charge details the death of 60-year-old Maya Islam and the injury of her 6-year-old grandson, Basit Khan Musa. A bullet fired by police passed through the child's head and hit Maya in the stomach, killing her.
The trial began on September 18 with charges framed against the high-ranking police officials. The injured survivor, Amir Hossain, provided a harrowing account of the shooting as the first witness.
The three-member judicial panel, led by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, will now decide the fate of the accused officers based on the evidence and arguments presented.
caption:
A youth hanging from a roof rod was shot six times. Two others were killed. Today, the International Crimes Tribunal delivers its verdict.

The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) is set to deliver its verdict today in a case involving crimes against humanity during the 2024 July Uprising in Dhaka's Rampura. The case centers on the shooting and killing of two people and the serious injury of another.

The charges involve five police officers, including former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman. While ASI Chanchal Chandra Sarkar is currently in jail, the other four accused officers are absconding.

One charge details the death of 38-year-old Md Nadeem, who was killed on July 19 when police opened fire indiscriminately in Banasree H Block. He was hit by two bullets in the stomach and back.

Another charge involves 18-year-old Amir Hossain, who sought shelter in an under-construction building to escape police fire. He was shot six times while hanging from a roof rod (cornice) after refusing to jump down.

A third charge details the death of 60-year-old Maya Islam and the injury of her 6-year-old grandson, Basit Khan Musa. A bullet fired by police passed through the child's head and hit Maya in the stomach, killing her.

The trial began on September 18 with charges framed against the high-ranking police officials. The injured survivor, Amir Hossain, provided a harrowing account of the shooting as the first witness.

The three-member judicial panel, led by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, will now decide the fate of the accused officers based on the evidence and arguments presented.
